title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 342
paragraphs: This Cheops, the Egyptians said, reigned for fifty years; and after he died, his brother Chephren succeeded to the kingdom. This king followed the same pattern as the other in every respect, including the fact that he built a pyramid. His pyramid did not reach the dimensions of the one built by his predecessor — I know this, having measured it myself — and moreover it has no underground chambers beneath it, nor does a channel from the Nile flow to it as to the other, where the water coming through a built conduit flows around an island within, and where they say Cheops himself is buried. But for a foundation he laid the first course in Ethiopian stone of varied colors. He built this pyramid forty feet lower than the other in size, placing it next to the great pyramid. The two stand on the same hill, which is about a hundred feet high. And Chephren, they said, reigned fifty-six years.
